items.title: Meta moves Health & Wellness ads to claims-based review
items.summary: Meta's updated Health & Wellness Advertising Standards took effect July 22, 2026, judging ads on their claims and intent rather than on the product category, which should cut false rejections for sexual health and contraception. Products that 'enhance sexual desire, arousal, or pleasure' are still prohibited, and sexual health ads must target 18+ and lead with health benefits.
items.sowhat: Rewrite paid copy around health, comfort and education claims such as dryness, pelvic health or menopause, keep pleasure language for organic posts, and re-submit ads that were rejected before July.

items.title: Instagram rolls out 13+ Teen Accounts worldwide
items.summary: Instagram is rolling out its movie-rating-inspired 13+ content setting internationally: under-18 accounts see no sexually suggestive or mature content by default, and parents can turn on a stricter Limited Content mode. Accounts that regularly post age-inappropriate content are filtered from teens.
items.sowhat: Expect less recommendation reach wherever Meta can't confirm a viewer's age, and keep Reels covers and captions non-suggestive so adult viewers still get them in Explore.

items.title: 13+ filter extends to Facebook and Messenger and applies to sponsored posts too
items.summary: A brand-reach analysis reports that Meta expanded the 13+ setting globally to Facebook and Messenger in June 2026 (exact day unconfirmed, so the 1st of the month is used here). The analysis says the filter applies to organic and paid-partnership content alike, and Meta has documented no exception for sponsored posts.
items.sowhat: Brief creators that a 'Paid partnership' label won't protect suggestive content from being filtered, and review creator whitelisting plans with that in mind.

items.title: TikTok branded content still bans sex toys and lube
items.summary: TikTok's Branded Content Policy still lists 'adult and sexual products' as prohibited, naming sex toys, lubricants and fetish costumes, while some contraceptives and medications are allowed. The policy page is undated; it was checked in September 2026, so the 1st of the month is used here.
items.sowhat: Keep TikTok creator deals product-free or education-led (anatomy, communication, myth-busting), and don't tag toys in paid partnerships.

items.title: TikTok Shop: lube and cycle care sell, explicit items don't
items.summary: An agency analysis finds that lubricants, consumables and reproductive and cycle-care products perform very well on TikTok Shop, while intimacy accessories do moderately well when framed as education. It says explicit or adult-only items are heavily restricted.
items.sowhat: If you test TikTok Shop, lead with lube and body-care SKUs and send traffic for devices to your own site.

items.title: YouTube uses AI to estimate viewers' ages in the US
items.summary: YouTube estimates viewer age from signals such as watch history, and accounts it treats as under 18 get non-personalized ads, restricted mature content and wellbeing reminders. Adults who are misclassified have to verify with a credit card or government ID.
items.sowhat: Age-restricted sex-ed videos will lose some adult viewers to misclassification, so make clean, non-restricted cuts and Shorts that lead into the full videos.

items.title: X tightens adult-content age assurance and advertiser adjacency defaults
items.summary: A third-party policy comparison, not an official X source, reports that X now excludes ads from appearing next to adult content by default and requires age assurance for EU and UK users who want to view adult content. It also says adult-labelled posts are de-indexed from search engines.
items.sowhat: Don't mark the brand account as sensitive, since X remains the most open platform for pleasure-forward copy but labelled posts lose discovery.

items.title: UK announces under-16 social media ban and age checks for all users
items.summary: The UK government announced on June 15, 2026 a ban on social media for under-16s, with regulations due by the end of 2026 and enforcement in spring 2027. Platforms including Instagram, TikTok, X and YouTube will need to verify the age of every user, adults included.
items.sowhat: Plan for a verified-adult UK audience from 2027, which could eventually loosen reach limits for 18+ content, and keep content age-gated until then.

items.title: Ofcom has issued £7m+ in Online Safety Act fines, mostly unpaid
items.summary: Ofcom has fined 11 providers more than £7 million under the Online Safety Act, most of them porn sites, but its enforcement director admits the majority of the fines haven't been paid. The regulator has 40 open investigations covering more than 100 services, including TikTok and X.
items.sowhat: Enforcement is aimed at porn, not wellness retail, but keep explicit imagery off UK-facing pages so the site isn't classed as a pornographic service.

items.title: Ofcom's biggest age-assurance fines to date: £1.35m and £800k
items.summary: In February 2026 Ofcom fined 8579 LLC £1.35 million and Kick Online Entertainment £800,000 for failing to put 'highly effective age assurance' in place. The regulator is enforcing across operators' whole site portfolios, not just single services.
items.sowhat: Check that any UK landing page carrying explicit or user-generated content sits behind proper age assurance, not a checkbox.

items.title: EU age-verification app is 'technically ready'
items.summary: On April 15, 2026 the European Commission said its privacy-preserving age-verification app is ready, with rollout tied to the EU Digital Identity Wallet by the end of 2026. Member states are also adding their own social media age limits, such as France's under-15 ban and Austria's under-14 limit.
items.sowhat: Budget for EU-compliant age checks on adult product pages in 2027, and plan EU social strategy country by country.

items.title: Supreme Court lets Texas app store age-verification law take effect
items.summary: The US Supreme Court declined to block Texas SB 2420, which requires Apple and Google to verify every user's age and get parental consent before minors download apps or make purchases. An expedited Fifth Circuit hearing on whether the law is constitutional was set for early August 2026.
items.sowhat: If the brand runs an app, such as for app-controlled toys, check that it has an 18+ rating and uses the new age-range APIs.

items.title: Apple enforces 18+ confirmation for Texas accounts
items.summary: From June 4, 2026, Texas users must confirm they are 18+ when creating an Apple Account, and minors need Family Sharing consent for every download and purchase. Developers must use Apple's Declared Age Range API and face civil penalties of up to $10,000 per violation.
items.sowhat: App-connected toy brands should confirm their App Store age category and consent flow for Texas now.

items.title: Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA tariffs, opening refunds for importers
items.summary: In a 6-3 ruling on February 20, 2026, the Supreme Court held that IEEPA does not let the President impose sweeping tariffs, which opened the door to an estimated $175 billion in refunds. Toy brands had been hit by these China tariffs in 2025, and Dame, for example, added a surcharge.
items.sowhat: If you raised prices because of tariffs, a 'price drop' or 'surcharge removed' post is a good-will message, but check with finance on refund status first.

items.title: plusOne vibrators land in 1,300+ Ulta stores
items.summary: plusOne, from Beacon Wellness Brands, launched massagers and intimate care products in more than 1,300 Ulta Beauty stores and online, which it calls the largest intimate wellness brand broadly carried by Ulta. Ulta-exclusive plusOne products are due in early 2027.
items.sowhat: Mass beauty retail is normalizing toys as self-care, so lean into beauty-shelf visuals (vanity shelfies, GRWM) and use retail availability as proof in social posts.

items.title: Mila raises $2.5M to sell intimate wellness as a beauty ritual
items.summary: Mila launched with $2.5 million in pre-seed funding from Mensch VC and Sticker Ventures, with the Aura 4-in-1 device, the Bloom intimate mist and a planned lube line built on K-beauty ingredients. Investors have otherwise been cool on sexual wellness since the 2020–21 peak.
items.sowhat: The skincare-ritual framing is how new entrants position themselves, so make sure your own content owns the 'self-care routine' angle first.

items.title: Sex tech back at CES 2026, led by Lovense
items.summary: Lovense exhibited at CES 2026 in Las Vegas on January 15, presenting itself as a leader in intimacy tech. CES rules for sex-tech exhibitors still ban overtly sexual language at booths.
items.sowhat: Use trade-show and 'tech' framing for connected products, since it gets through platform filters better than pleasure framing.

items.title: Womanizer brings sexual wellness to IFA Berlin
items.summary: Womanizer exhibited at IFA 2026 (September 4–8), Europe's biggest consumer electronics fair, showing Next Liberty and the award-winning Snap, which launches September 22. It also ran a Creator Stage session titled 'Why Pleasure is the ultimate Beauty Tech'.
items.sowhat: Competitors are claiming 'beauty tech' in mainstream venues, so decide whether to own that positioning or counter it.

items.title: Womanizer Beauty: a lipstick-shaped toy made for the vanity
items.summary: Womanizer relaunched its lipstick-style 2GO as Womanizer Beauty ($79) in four colours, available in Europe from July 14 and in North America from September 22. The brand says the discreet design is so pleasure 'can belong naturally in everyday spaces'.
items.sowhat: Expect a wave of 'what's in my makeup bag' reveals, and get ahead with your own discreet-design content.

items.title: LELO report predicts an 'analogue counter-movement' in intimacy
items.summary: LELO's 2026 Futurist Report, written with Tracey Follows, finds 60% of people have used AI in their intimate lives, and 18% of Americans have passed off AI-written messages as their own. It predicts a move toward phone-free bedrooms and 'protected human presence'.
items.sowhat: Build a phone-free / offline intimacy content series, which makes a strong counterpoint to AI companion discourse.

items.title: Lovehoney's 2026 sex trends: purposeful pleasure, playful toys, Gen X
items.summary: Lovehoney's report names seven trends, among them Purposeful Pleasure (Gen Z choosing intentional sex), Playful Pleasure (cute, collectible toys), Generation (se)X and Cosmic Pleasure (astrology). It also finds 18% of Gen Z and millennials admit to using their phones during sex.
items.sowhat: Aim more content at Gen X, which has high confidence and is underserved, and try collectible and astrology formats with younger audiences.

items.title: Lovehoney's US 'Sex Map' turns sales data into shareable stats
items.summary: Lovehoney published an interactive map from 12 months of sales, naming Vermont the 'sexiest state', Boston the top city and Arlington, VA the 'kinkiest'. Fun stats such as dildo purchases stretching past 120 Statues of Liberty drove press coverage.
items.sowhat: Mine your own anonymized sales data for local, shareable stat posts, which fit X and local-pride formats well.

items.title: Lovehoney opens Q4 early with five 2026 advent calendars
items.summary: Lovehoney launched five advent calendars ($129–$369) in August, featuring Womanizer and We-Vibe toys, and positioned them as selling out fast. The exact launch day is unconfirmed, so the 1st of the month is used here.
items.sowhat: Advent and gifting content is already live at competitors, so start your holiday gift-guide content in October, not November.

items.title: Satisfyer sails a Pro 2-shaped boat at WorldPride Amsterdam
items.summary: Satisfyer sponsored a boat modelled on its Satisfyer Pro 2 in the WorldPride Amsterdam Canal Parade on August 1, 2026. It carried the message that everyone deserves pleasure 'without shame, without limits, and without exclusion'.
items.sowhat: Plan physical, photogenic activations tied to cultural moments, which travel well on IG and TikTok without showing product explicitly.
